content.intro: This lesson focuses on resource identifiers in resource modeling and url design. You will connect sequential ids, uuids, and opaque identifiers to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: Resource Identifiers matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying sequential ids, uuids, and opaque identifiers deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: A resource is identified independently from the code or database row that implements it; a stable URI names the target. In this lesson, treat “Resource Identifiers” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.

content_blocks.title: Walkthrough
content_blocks.text: Start with “Sequential IDs, UUIDs, and opaque identifiers”; it establishes the vocabulary for this topic.
